script: She bargained for a whole bolt—now my boss is furious and my life's ruined.. I was juggling fabric scraps in the backroom, not even a pro at cutting. A customer—let's call her "Sally"—walks in and drops two questions I can't answer because the fabric crew are out. She spots a bolt, decides she wants the whole thing, 4¾ yards. I am already half‑stressed from messing up her orders before, so I am like, "Sure, we can do 4½ yards and you'll clear the extra ¼." I measure, line it up, and snap a clean cut. She looks at me, eyes wide, and goes, "NO! Don't cut it!" I am like, "What?!" I forgot all about customer service for a sec and blurted, "You can't have 4¾ for the price of 4½!!" (I mean, if you say 4½, I am assuming that's the total length, not a discount on the full bolt). It was literally insane—here I was, about to cut the fabric, and she's like, "Hold up, no cutting." I am left staring at a half‑cut bolt, realizing I just dropped the ball on a simple request. (I know, right?)
